\chapter{Beautiful, Far and Near}
\label{ch:sa-beautiful-far-near}
\hlchaptermodality{89}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say something is beautiful, far, near, hard or sweet.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 89: i can say something is beautiful, far, near, hard or sweet.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[sundaraḥ]{\sk{सुन्दरः} (sundaraḥ) — beautiful}

\label{lesson:SA-C89-beautiful}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a son, then the Sanskrit for a daughter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{सुन्दरः}}
\textbf{\sk{सुन्दरः}} (\emph{sundaraḥ}) — \textquotedblleft{}beautiful\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\sk{सुन्दरः} \sk{मयूरः}} — \textquotedblleft{}a beautiful peacock\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Before the noun, and it agrees.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sundaraḥ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sundaraḥ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{sundaraḥ mayūraḥ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for a son, then the Sanskrit for a daughter, then say \emph{sundaraḥ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{सुन्दरः} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Beautiful\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[dūram]{\sk{दूरम्} (dūram) — far}

\label{lesson:SA-C89-far}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a daughter, then the Sanskrit for beautiful.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{दूरम्}}
\textbf{\sk{दूरम्}} (\emph{dūram}) — \textquotedblleft{}far\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\sk{विद्यालयः} \sk{दूरम्}} — \textquotedblleft{}the school is far\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
How far away it is.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dūram}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dūram}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{dūram}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for a daughter, then the Sanskrit for beautiful, then say \emph{dūram} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{दूरम्} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Far\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[samīpam]{\sk{समीपम्} (samīpam) — near}

\label{lesson:SA-C89-near}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for beautiful, then the Sanskrit for far.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{समीपम्}}
\textbf{\sk{समीपम्}} (\emph{samīpam}) — \textquotedblleft{}near\textquotedblright{}, the opposite of \textbf{\sk{दूरम्}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The other side of far.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{samīpam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{samīpam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{samīpam}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for beautiful, then the Sanskrit for far, then say \emph{samīpam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{समीपम्} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Near\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kaṭhinaḥ]{\sk{कठिनः} (kaṭhinaḥ) — hard, difficult}

\label{lesson:SA-C89-hard}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for far, then the Sanskrit for near.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{कठिनः}}
\textbf{\sk{कठिनः}} (\emph{kaṭhinaḥ}) — \textquotedblleft{}hard\textquotedblright{}, both to touch and to do. \textbf{\sk{कठिनः} \sk{पाठः}} — \textquotedblleft{}a hard lesson\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
What a hard lesson is.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṭhinaḥ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṭhinaḥ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{kaṭhinaḥ pāṭhaḥ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for far, then the Sanskrit for near, then say \emph{kaṭhinaḥ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{कठिनः} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Hard, difficult\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[madhuraḥ]{\sk{मधुरः} (madhuraḥ) — sweet}

\label{lesson:SA-C89-sweet}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for near, then the Sanskrit for hard.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{मधुरः}}
\textbf{\sk{मधुरः}} (\emph{madhuraḥ}) — \textquotedblleft{}sweet\textquotedblright{}, from \textbf{\sk{मधु}}, \textquotedblleft{}honey\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\sk{मधुरम्} \sk{आम्रम्}} — \textquotedblleft{}a sweet mango\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Honey, as a describing word.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{madhuraḥ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{madhuraḥ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{madhuram āmram}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for near, then the Sanskrit for hard, then say \emph{madhuraḥ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{मधुरः} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Sweet\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Fruit, animals and the land — a first pass}

\label{lesson:SA-R89-first-pass-food-animals-nature}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}a hard lesson\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}a sweet mango\textquotedblright{}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a mango, a banana, oil, flatbread, sweet rice pudding
  \item an elephant, a horse, a camel, a mouse, a cat
  \item a crow, a parrot, a peacock, a tortoise, a frog
  \item a tree, a seed, a root, a garden, a forest
  \item a lake, a well, a pond, an island, a river bank
  \item a school, a student, a teacher, a lesson, an exam
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Mango, banana, oil, bread, pudding? (\textbf{\sk{आम्रम्}, \sk{कदलीफलम्}, \sk{तैलम्}, \sk{रोटिका}, \sk{पायसम्}}.) Elephant, horse, camel, mouse, cat? (\textbf{\sk{गजः}, \sk{अश्वः}, \sk{उष्ट्रः}, \sk{मूषकः}, \sk{मार्जारः}}.) Crow, parrot, peacock, tortoise, frog? (\textbf{\sk{काकः}, \sk{शुकः}, \sk{मयूरः}, \sk{कूर्मः}, \sk{मण्डूकः}}.) Tree, seed, root, garden, forest? (\textbf{\sk{वृक्षः}, \sk{बीजम्}, \sk{मूलम्}, \sk{उद्यानम्}, \sk{अरण्यम्}}.) Lake, well, pond, island, shore? (\textbf{\sk{सरः}, \sk{कूपः}, \sk{तडागः}, \sk{द्वीपः}, \sk{तीरम्}}.) School, student, teacher, lesson, exam? (\textbf{\sk{विद्यालयः}, \sk{छात्रः}, \sk{अध्यापकः}, \sk{पाठः}, \sk{परीक्षा}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Places, days and people — a second pass}

\label{lesson:SA-R89-second-pass-places-days-people}



\begin{quote}
Ask where the temple is, then where the hospital is.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a field, a farmer, a merchant
  \item a week; Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday
  \item Friday, Saturday, Sunday; ask the time; one moment
  \item eleven, twelve, twenty, a hundred, a thousand
  \item a girl, a young man, my friend (a woman's), my son, my daughter
  \item a beautiful peacock; far; near; a hard lesson; a sweet mango
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Temple, hospital, field, farmer, merchant? (\textbf{\sk{मन्दिरम्}, \sk{चिकित्सालयः}, \sk{क्षेत्रम्}, \sk{कृषकः}, \sk{वणिक्}}.) Week? (\textbf{\sk{सप्ताहः}}.) Monday to Sunday? (\textbf{\sk{सोमवासरः}, \sk{मंगलवासरः}, \sk{बुधवासरः}, \sk{गुरुवासरः}, \sk{शुक्रवासरः}, \sk{शनिवासरः}, \sk{रविवासरः}}.) Time, moment? (\textbf{\sk{समयः}, \sk{क्षणः}}.) Eleven, twelve, twenty, hundred, thousand? (\textbf{\sk{एकादश}, \sk{द्वादश}, \sk{विंशतिः}, \sk{शतम्}, \sk{सहस्रम्}}.) Girl, young man, friend, son, daughter? (\textbf{\sk{बालिका}, \sk{युवकः}, \sk{सखी}, \sk{पुत्रः}, \sk{पुत्री}}.) Beautiful, far, near, hard, sweet? (\textbf{\sk{सुन्दरः}, \sk{दूरम्}, \sk{समीपम्}, \sk{कठिनः}, \sk{मधुरः}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
